scope: Wedding naming, media influence and practical cultural transmission: source review and editorial guidance

sources.title: With So Many New Age Additions, Odia Weddings Are Truly Witnessing A Makeover!
sources.author: Dikhya Mohanty
sources.classification: Local reported lifestyle feature containing named interviews plus reporter interpretation
sources.locators: Author/date lines30–32; Smita Choudhury lines50–51; Pratishruti Mohanty line53; venue manager Abinash Sahu lines62–66
sources.supported_claim: In 2016 MyCityLinks interviewed Cuttack residents about added sangeet, mehendi and bachelor-party functions. One parent attributed demands to peers and media; another interviewee welcomed greater choice. A venue manager described clients asking for film-themed decoration.
sources.limits: These are reported participant experiences and industry observations, not representative prevalence measurements or demonstrated media causality. The reporter’s compressed two-ritual wedding history is not a reliable complete ritual inventory. The article does not establish systematic renaming of Odia rites.

sources.title: Band, Baja, Baraat – Then and Now
sources.author: Neha Jha
sources.classification: Reported local feature; named interviews and untested interpretive claims
sources.locators: Byline/date lines28–30; Kalindi Nayak lines38–39; Sipra Singh lines40–42; reporter Bollywood/TV discussion line49
sources.supported_claim: The 2019 feature records Sipra Singh contrasting her wedding with a niece’s longer celebration containing sangeet and a separate mehndi day. Sociologist Kalindi Nayak attributed wedding changes to social and popular media.
sources.limits: Attribution is the interviewee’s interpretation, not a causal study. Claims that most weddings include these additions and that television caused adoption are not backed by a survey here. A December-last-year reference to the Anushka Sharma–Virat Kohli wedding is chronologically inconsistent with the displayed 2019 date; avoid deriving a trend timeline from it. No proof that established Odia names were replaced.

sources.title: Big, fat Odia weddings
sources.author: Diana Sahu
sources.publication_date_note: Inspected page labels this Updated on, not separately Published on
sources.classification: Reported feature on affluent wedding market, named couples and commercial stakeholders; quantitative estimates not independently audited
sources.locators: Author in standfirst line42; updated lines48–50; Brij Mohan Agarwal line66; choreographed wedding line69; photographer Boon Patnaik lines72–73; Swadesh Patra line85
sources.supported_claim: The report describes separate haldi, mehndi and sangeet events and film-song performances at a named wedding. A photographer thought photo opportunities encouraged additions; another couple said modern elements coexisted with their Odia rites.
sources.limits: Photographer’s explanation is explicitly opinion. Addition of a separately staged haldi event does not establish turmeric use as foreign or newly introduced. The report supports coexistence as well as change. Do not use industry spending totals, counts or destination shares as verified population statistics; no statewide sample or method is supplied.

sources.title: An “Arranged Love” Marriage: India’s Neoliberal Turn and the Bollywood Wedding Culture Industry
sources.author: Jyotsna Kapur
sources.access: Publisher abstract and bibliographic metadata inspected; full article not accessed
sources.locator: Wiley metadata lines15–39 and173–177; Abstract lines65–68; OUP metadata lines15–18
sources.supported_claim: Kapur interprets lavish wedding culture in relation to Bollywood, economic liberalisation and the professional wedding industry. This supplies a wider analytical frame for the local reporting.
sources.limits: Not Odisha-specific; not evidence of measured naming displacement or a causal estimate. Cite the abstract as the inspected scope. Distinguish June issue date from July online publication. Direct DOI resolver failed, but publisher landing pages were accessible.

synthesis: Local reporting provides dated examples of added wedding functions, screen-inspired presentation and participants who attribute changes to media. It does not establish statewide replacement of Odia names. The evidence also records personal choice and coexistence with Odia rituals.
recommended_editorial_action: Use attributed, dated examples followed by a constructive suggestion: label established family rites in Odia, explain them to guests, and clearly distinguish optional added festivities. Do not claim a universal one-to-one equivalence between mangana and every event called haldi without further ritual-specific evidence.
forbidden_inferences: Bollywood causes statewide Odia cultural decline
Sangeet or mehndi replaced every traditional Odia rite
Haldi means turmeric was foreign to Odisha
A commercial event label alone proves an older name has disappeared
An affluent urban wedding sample represents all Odisha families

guidance.risk: Using a generic ring-ceremony label without explaining the family observance
guidance.action: Retain Nirbandha when the family is performing that rite; explain it rather than equating every ring exchange with it.

guidance.risk: Treating every staged haldi event as equivalent to local Mangana, or claiming turmeric use is foreign
guidance.action: Document the local name, sequence and family/community context; distinguish it from any additional themed celebration.

guidance.risk: Presenting a participant opinion about films as proof of statewide cultural displacement
guidance.action: Attribute interview views; preserve examples of coexistence and choice.

guidance.risk: Replacing Navaratri with Vijaya Dashami as though both name the same duration
guidance.action: Distinguish nine nights from tenth day; use the appropriate local name for the actual observance.

guidance.risk: Letting a generic event template omit family names and songs
guidance.action: Use Odia labels with explanations, invite willing relatives to teach songs, and credit teachers.
